blocks.text: This chapter introduces computer networks: how devices are connected and how they communicate. It covers network architecture and its basic working, the main types of network, networking devices (NICs, switches, routers, modems and access points), topologies, the OSI model, common protocols (TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP and DNS), IP addressing, subnetting and NAT, home network setup and Wi-Fi security, diagnostic commands such as ping and ipconfig, and finally network performance, security, backup and the balance between usability and security.

blocks.title: Computer network
blocks.text: A computer network is a group of connected computers and other devices that communicate with each other to share data, resources and services.

A network lets different devices connect and communicate, so information can be shared quickly and easily, which saves time and effort. Networks can connect computers, mobile phones, printers and other digital devices (Fig 1.1). The devices communicate through cables or wireless signals, and data, files and resources move from one device to another. Networks can be small or large depending on the need, and they are used in homes, schools, offices and businesses; modern life depends heavily on them.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Networks support online learning and remote work, and businesses rely on networks for their daily operations.

items: Internet browsing is a common example of network use.
Mobile phones use networks for calls, messages and apps.
Schools use networks for online classes and learning systems.
Banks use networks for online transactions and ATMs.
Social media platforms work through computer networks.
Smart homes use networks to control devices.
